title.narrative: Social protection (system, benefits and access) expanded, in particular among workers in the informal economy, and to men, women, youth and vulnerable groups in Cambodia

description.narrative: The CPO KHM226 addresses the critical challenge of sustaining Cambodia’s human development gains by advancing social protection systems that are inclusive, resilient, and capable of withstanding economic and external shocks. Despite substantial progress in poverty reduction, with the rate falling from 47.8% in 2007 to 13.5% in 2014, and the achievement of lower middle-income status in 2015, Cambodia remains vulnerable due to its narrow economic base, high informality, dollarized economy, and limited social safety nets. Around 4.5 million people are still poor and at risk of falling back into poverty, while nearly half of Cambodian children experience multidimensional deprivation. During the biennium, the CPO supports the Royal Government of Cambodia’s efforts to strengthen and expand social protection coverage, particularly for informal and vulnerable workers. This includes enhancing the design, implementation, and monitoring of the National Social Protection Policy Framework (NSPPF) 2016–2025. The programme contributes to building the robust evidence base and monitoring and evaluation systems to inform decision-making, improve programme delivery, and advocate for greater public investment in social protection. The primary beneficiaries of this work are vulnerable populations, including informal workers, near-poor households, and children facing multiple deprivations. National institutions such as the National Social Protection Council and its General Secretariat also benefit from capacity building and technical support. The strategy is implemented in close coordination with government ministries and international development partners, including multilateral and bilateral agencies. Aligned with ILO’s global mandate on comprehensive social protection and relevant international standards, the programme aims to ensure income security, promote welfare, and support Cambodia’s ambition to achieve upper-middle-income status by 2030.
